correctness.rationale: The inradius defect vanishes for each cocircular quadruple by the Japanese theorem. At a regular n-gon, radial differentiation yields the exactly four-tap Jacobian κ[−I+(1+2cos h)S−(1+2cos h)S²+S³], factoring as κ(S−I)(S−e^ih I)(S−e^-ih I). The circle translation/radius tangent modes 0,±1 form its complete 3D kernel. On Fourier k its singular value is 8κ|sin(kx)sin((k−1)x)sin((k+1)x)|. For 2≤k≤floor(n/2) this is increasing by s(s²−sin²x), so k=2,n−2 are least positive; μn=4 sin x sin 2x sin 3x/[cos x(1+cos x)(1+2cos x)]∼4π³/n³. Rank n−3, implicit-function uniqueness, and a tubular nearest circle point yield local F=0 iff cocircular and the sharp distance/error limit. Independently differentiated inradius numerically at n=4,5,7,10,16 and reproduced the Jacobian and gap; exact symbolic identity in supplied verification was inspected, not treated as proof alone.
residual_risks: Local in radial near-regular strictly convex configurations with fixed n; no uniform neighborhood in n or global converse.
